beats.title: Eridu Is Settled
beats.description: Farmers settle the marshy southern plain at Eridu, which Sumerians later remembered as the oldest city of their land.

beats.title: Uruk Becomes the First City
beats.description: Uruk grows into a walled urban centre with temples and thousands of residents, the largest settlement in the world.

beats.title: Cuneiform Writing Emerges
beats.description: Scribes press wedge-shaped marks into wet clay tablets to record grain, beer and temple goods, the first writing.
beats.note: Proto-cuneiform dated c. 3350-3200 BC; conventional 3200 used

beats.title: The Royal Tombs of Ur Are Filled
beats.description: Rulers of a Sumerian city are buried with lyres, gold headdresses and attendants in richly furnished underground tombs.
beats.note: Royal tombs c. 2600-2500 BC; start used

beats.title: Urukagina Issues Reforms at Lagash
beats.description: A Sumerian king curbs corrupt officials and protects widows and the poor in what is often called the first recorded reform.
beats.note: Sources vary c. 2378-2340 BC; c. 2350 used

beats.title: Sargon of Akkad Founds His Empire
beats.description: A cupbearer-turned-king unites the Sumerian city-states under Akkadian rule, building the first empire.

beats.title: Enheduanna Writes Her Hymns
beats.description: A priestess and daughter of a king composes hymns to the goddess Inanna, becoming the first author known by name.

beats.title: Naram-Sin Raises His Victory Stele
beats.description: A king depicts himself climbing a mountain over fallen enemies and takes the title King of the Four Quarters.
beats.note: Sources give c. 2254-2218 BC (reign) or c. 2250; start of reign used

beats.title: The Code of Ur-Nammu
beats.description: A Sumerian king issues the oldest surviving law code, setting fines in silver for injuries and other offences.

beats.title: Elamites Sack the City of Ur
beats.description: Raiders from the east capture Ur and carry off its king, ending the last great Sumerian dynasty.

beats.title: An Amorite Dynasty Takes Babylon
beats.description: A chieftain founds a ruling house in a small river town that will grow into the most famous city of Mesopotamia.

beats.title: Plimpton 322 Is Inscribed
beats.description: A clay tablet lists number sets that match right triangles, showing advanced mathematics long before the Greeks.

beats.title: Hammurabi Takes the Throne
beats.description: A young king inherits the minor kingdom of Babylon and begins conquests that will unify southern Mesopotamia.

beats.title: Hammurabi Destroys Mari
beats.description: Babylon's king defeats his former ally and razes its palace city on the Euphrates, ending a rival power.

beats.title: The Code of Hammurabi Is Carved
beats.description: Nearly three hundred laws, including an eye for an eye, are inscribed on a black stone pillar for all to read.

beats.title: Hittites Sack Babylon
beats.description: A raiding army from Anatolia plunders the capital and carries off the statue of its chief god, ending Hammurabi's dynasty.

beats.title: Ashur-uballit I Frees Assyria
beats.description: An Assyrian king writes to the pharaoh as an equal and frees his city from Mitanni overlordship, starting an empire.

beats.title: Tukulti-Ninurta I Conquers Babylon
beats.description: An Assyrian king defeats the Babylonian ruler and takes the great southern city, the first time Assyria rules it.
beats.note: Search gives c. 1225; a later looting is dated c. 1217

beats.title: Elam Carries Off Hammurabi's Stele
beats.description: Invaders from the east topple Babylon's ruling dynasty and haul away its famed monuments, including the law pillar.

beats.title: Nebuchadnezzar I Recovers Marduk
beats.description: A Babylonian king invades Elam and brings back the stolen statue of the city's chief god, making Marduk supreme.
beats.note: Battle c. 1120 BC; story possibly later tradition

beats.title: Tiglath-Pileser I Expands Assyria
beats.description: A warrior king marches his army to the Mediterranean coast and Lake Van, restoring Assyrian strength after a long decline.

beats.title: Gilgamesh Epic Takes Final Form
beats.description: A scribe gathers older Sumerian tales of a king seeking immortality into the long poem that includes a great flood.
beats.note: Standard Babylonian version compiled between 1300 and 1000 BC; c. 1100 used, approximate

beats.title: Ashurnasirpal II Builds Nimrud
beats.description: An Assyrian king moves his capital to Kalhu and celebrates with a feast for some seventy thousand guests.

beats.title: Battle of Qarqar
beats.description: A king of Assyria faces a league of western rulers in Syria, leaving the earliest mention of Israel in an Assyrian record.

beats.title: Babylon Starts Its Sky Diaries
beats.description: Priests of Babylon start systematic records of the heavens that will be kept for centuries and used by later scholars.
beats.note: Era of Nabonassar, 747 BC; oldest surviving diaries date from 652 BC

beats.title: Tiglath-Pileser III Revives Assyria
beats.description: A usurper seizes the throne, reforms the army and provinces and launches a new age of Assyrian conquest.
beats.note: Took the throne 745 after revolt in 746

beats.title: Assyria Conquers Israel
beats.description: Assyrian forces take the northern capital of Samaria and deport many of its people, the origin of the lost tribes.
beats.note: Fall of Samaria 722; some scholars place Sargon's deportation c. 720

beats.title: Sargon II Founds Dur-Sharrukin
beats.description: An Assyrian king buys farmland and begins a vast new capital with a palace, only to see it abandoned after his death.
beats.note: Construction began 717 per most sources; Oracc says 713

beats.title: Sennacherib Finishes Nineveh Palace
beats.description: An Assyrian king boasts that his Palace Without Rival at Nineveh is complete, with an aqueduct and gardens.

beats.title: Esarhaddon Conquers Egypt
beats.description: An Assyrian army marches across the desert and takes Memphis, adding the Nile valley to the empire.

beats.title: Ashurbanipal Takes the Throne
beats.description: The last great Assyrian king succeeds his father, trained as a scribe as well as a warrior, as the empire reaches its widest extent.
beats.note: Late 669 per Wikipedia; some sources give 668

beats.title: Nabopolassar Founds New Babylonia
beats.description: A Chaldean general takes the throne of Babylon and breaks free of Assyrian rule, starting a new Babylonian empire.

beats.title: The Fall of Nineveh
beats.description: Babylonians and Medes storm the great Assyrian capital and burn it, ending the Assyrian empire.

beats.title: Nebuchadnezzar Wins at Carchemish
beats.description: A Babylonian prince crushes the Egyptian and Assyrian remnant on the Euphrates, giving Babylon mastery of the Near East.

beats.title: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon
beats.description: Nebuchadnezzar is said to have built terraced gardens for his homesick queen, later counted among the Seven Wonders.
beats.note: Traditional, within Nebuchadnezzar II's reign (605-562); existence and date debated

beats.title: Nebuchadnezzar Takes Jerusalem
beats.description: Babylon's king captures the city of Judah, carries off its king and treasures and installs a puppet ruler.

beats.title: The Babylonian Exile Begins
beats.description: After Jerusalem's temple is destroyed, thousands of Judeans are marched to Babylon to live in captivity.

beats.title: The Ishtar Gate Is Built
beats.description: Babylon's northern entrance is faced with glazed blue bricks and rows of lions, bulls and dragons.

beats.title: Babylon Falls to Cyrus
beats.description: The Persian army enters the city almost without a fight, ending the last native Mesopotamian empire.
beats.note: Included as the end of Babylonian rule
